title: Infinite trees: branches, König's lemma, and Aronszajn trees

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 68–69 (§16, Lemma 16.1 and Theorem 16.3; finite repair and fresh reserves supplied explicitly)

summary: Trees with nonempty finite levels indexed by the natural numbers have an infinite path; countable levels at uncountable height need not give a path through every level.
abstract: Finite decreasing sequences of natural numbers can be arbitrarily long, although they cannot be extended compatibly into one infinite sequence. Regard each sequence as a node, and put it below every sequence that extends it. This forms a tree, with the length giving its level. König's lemma says that a tree with nonempty finite levels numbered by the natural numbers has a path through all of them. At the first uncountable height, countable levels need not give a path reaching every level. Such a counterexample is an Aronszajn tree; in the construction here, every individual node still extends to every higher level.
